transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Well, I’m here because lately... I don't know, I’ll get off a long shift at the shop or finish up studying, and I just end up eating way more than I ever planned to. Like, I'll put away a full fast-food meal, and then go after snacks, and basically whatever else is sitting in the fridge. Just all in one sitting. It's becoming a problem, so I figured I should talk to somebody about it.
After one of these episodes where you eat a large amount, do you ever try to make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, skipping meals afterward, or exercising a lot to compensate?

Yeah, I do. Most weeks, usually at least one night, I'll have one of those episodes where I just eat everything. And then... yeah, I try to make up for it. Sometimes I make myself throw up, or I'll take laxatives. Other times I'll just skip meals the next day or go hit the gym really hard to try and burn it off. It's been happening like this for a few months now.
During those episodes when you eat that much, do you feel like you can't stop or control what or how much you're eating, even if you want to?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start on those nights, it's like... I just can't stop. It feels like my hands just keep grabbing food, even while I'm telling myself to quit. Like, I'll even be feeling sick to my stomach, but I just keep going anyway. It's like I have no control over it at all.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports recurrent episodes of eating an objectively large amount of food in a discrete period with a subjective sense of loss of control, occurring at least once weekly for several months. These binges are followed by compensatory behaviors including self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, fasting, and excessive exercise aimed at preventing weight gain. This pattern of binge-purge cycles with loss of control and compensatory behavior over a multi-month duration meets criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2) rather than Binge-Eating Disorder (no compensatory behaviors) or unspecified feeding/eating disorder.

confirmed_symptoms: Eating an unusually large amount of food (fast food meal plus snacks and additional food) in a single sitting
Sense of loss of control during eating episodes ('can't stop', 'hands just keep grabbing food')
Continuing to eat despite physical discomfort (feeling sick to stomach)
Laxative use to compensate for binges
Excessive/intense exercise to 'burn off' calories after binges
